audit.reasoning: Coding: fixed-dominant, final (rule 01 001 0001...), strict=false. Nonato 2014 pp. 77 and 130 say main stress falls on the last UNDERLYING syllable, secondary stress iambic, clitics unstressed, and post-stress epenthetic echo vowels yield surface penultimate stress in coda-final words (/ˈtʰɛp/ -> [ˈtʰɛwɛ]); that is exactly dominant-but-not-exceptionless final stress, so the classification stands. The quotation is verbatim at the stated sections; the record's empty cite/loc/grade fields should be filled (Nonato 2014, sec. 4.4 p. 77; App. A.1.5 p. 130) now that the PDF is in custody. Guedes 1993 (fetched sources, pp. 72-73, 82) calls stress a 'suprasegmental phoneme' on the strength of toá 'dente' vs tóa 'banho' and a few paroxytones, while also reporting (via Steinen) that most words are final-stressed; her non-final cases are the kind Nonato derives from epenthesis, so this refines rather than

sources.citation: Nonato 2014 MIT thesis PDF (rafaeln.github.io/papers/), sec. 4.4 and App. A.1.5, full text extracted
sources.quote: Stress is iambic, with main stress falling on the last underlying syllable of stressed words (158). [...] Main stress falls on the last syllable of the underlying form of a stressable words. [...] Secondary stress is iambic.

sources.citation: Guedes, Marymarcia. 1993. Suyá: a língua da gente, um estudo fonológico e gramatical. Tese de doutorado, UNICAMP, Campinas. 277 pp. DOI 10.47749/t/unicamp.1993.62541
sources.quote: p. 72: 'a tonicidade é um fonema supra-segmental que tem sua realização na sílaba: /t.oá/ "dente" / /t.óa/ "banho" ... Os morfemas da Língua Suyá são geralmente monossilábicos ... Há, porém, a ocorrência de morfemas e palavras paroxítonas e até proparoxítonas' (exx. kumeni [kume'ni] 'muito'); p. 73: 'A realização fonética mais típica do acento é a duração mais longa da sílaba tônica'; p. 81: 'Steinen observa que, na maioria das palavras, o acento tônico ocorre na última sílaba'; p. 82: 'mostro que o acento é fonêmico na língua: toá "dente"/ tóa "banho"'.
sources.locator: sec. 2.8 'A Tonicidade em Suyá' pp. 72-73; sec. 2.11 pp. 81-82; p. 95

sources.citation: Nonato, Rafael. 2014. Clause-chaining, switch-reference and coordination. PhD dissertation, MIT. 152 pp. (rafaeln.github.io/papers/)
sources.quote: p. 77: 'Stress is iambic, with main stress falling on the last underlying syllable of stressed words (158). Clitics ... don't bear either primary or secondary stress.' p. 130: 'Main stress falls on the last syllable of the underlying form of a stressable words. ... The epenthesis process ... only happens after stress assignment though it changes the surface number of syllables of a word, it doesn't alter stress placement. (284) a. /ˈpəɲ/ -> [ˈpəji] ... d. /ˈtʰɛp/ -> [ˈtʰɛwɛ]'; '(285) Secondary stress is iambic.'

sources.citation: Guedes, Marymarcia. 1990. Uma proposta de análise do sistema fonológico do Suyá. Alfa 34: 143-151.
sources.quote: Explicitly restricted to vowel and consonant segments ('restringindo-se a análise unicamente aos segmentos vocálicos e consonantais'); silent on stress.

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. 595 pp.
sources.quote: No statement of Kĩsêdjê word stress. p. 9 ranks the sources: uses Santos (1997) and Nonato (2014); Guedes (1993) and Rodrigues & Ferreira-Silva (2011) 'não utilizamos amplamente ... em razão de problemas de transcrição fonológica'. pp. 52-53 describe Jê echo vowels as predictable post-coda vowels transcribed unstressed ([ˈkɤpɤ̆]), consistent with Nonato's underlying-final analysis.
